documents.title: Hematology-Oncology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Mr. Jackson has completed four cycles of daratumumab, bortezomib and dexamethasone for relapsed kappa light-chain myeloma with cast nephropathy.

Response is good: serum free kappa has fallen from 1,860 to 96 mg/L. Creatinine has improved to 3.6. He tolerates treatment with some fatigue and dex-day insomnia. No neuropathy so far. Adherence to tenofovir and acyclovir has been good by his report and pill counts.

Plan: complete eight cycles, then reassess for maintenance.

Hematology-Oncology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual.

Mid-way through myeloma treatment, cycle 5. Light chains down a lot per oncology. Tired, still working most days from home on infusion weeks. Dex nights still rough.
Taking tenofovir every day - pill box with alarms. Swelling much better.
Substance use: denies heroin or cocaine. Still smoking about a pack.

Meds: acyclovir 400 BID, dex 20 mg per cycle days, dara/bortezomib at clinic, tenofovir DF 300, amlodipine 5, metoprolol succinate 25, furosemide 40. NKDA.

Exam: BP 132/82. Weight 84. Heart regular, no gallop. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Trace ankle edema.
PHQ-2 2 - says it's the treatment grind, not depression; declined PHQ-9 today.

A/P
- Relapsed myeloma on DVd - per oncology.
- Cast nephropathy / FSGS, CKD 4 - CMP today.
- Hep B - tenofovir; LFTs.
- Paroxysmal AF - no recurrence, metoprolol.
- HTN - fine.
- Tobacco - counseled.
- HM: vaccines up to date (flu/COVID 10/2023, PCV20, Shingrix).

RTC 4 months.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 110. ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF.

Access: right radial artery. Left main: normal. LAD: no significant disease. Circumflex: no significant disease. RCA: dominant; thrombotic total occlusion of the mid segment, TIMI 0 flow. reports.conclusion: Single-vessel coronary disease: acute thrombotic occlusion of the mid RCA treated with one drug-eluting stent.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness. LVEF 50%. Hypokinesis of the inferior wall. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Prior mitral valve repair, intact, with mild mitral regurgitation and no stenosis. Aortic valve normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 50% with inferior hypokinesis. Intact mitral repair with mild regurgitation.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED NOTE - STEMI ALERT

40M brought from a party with crushing central chest pressure that started about half an hour before arrival, with palpitations and a feeling that something terrible was happening. History of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, mitral valve repair, hypertension. Says he uses cocaine now and then and used some earlier tonight.

BP 170/100, HR 110, RR 20, T 37.2. Agitated, pupils dilated. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular.

ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF. Cath lab activated on arrival.
Given aspirin 324 mg chewed, heparin bolus, lorazepam 2 mg IV for agitation, nitroglycerin. Beta-blocker held acutely with cocaine on board.
Troponin sent - pending at transfer to cath lab.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admitted 11/05/2024 - discharged 11/08/2024

Diagnosis: inferior STEMI, cocaine-associated. Single-vessel CAD.

Course: Emergent catheterization via right radial: thrombotic occlusion of the mid RCA, aspiration and one drug-eluting stent with TIMI 3 flow. Peak troponin I 38 ng/mL. Echo: LVEF 50% with inferior hypokinesis; mitral repair intact with mild MR. Contrast minimized; creatinine stayed at his baseline in the mid 3s. Ticagrelor loaded. No arrhythmia on telemetry. Daratumumab maintenance to resume per oncology after discharge.

Counseling: cocaine caused this heart attack and can cause another; strongly advised to stop. Smoking cessation advised.

Discharge medications:
- NEW aspirin 81 mg daily
- NEW ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily - do not stop without talking to cardiology
- NEW atorvastatin 80 mg nightly
- NEW nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed
- CHANGED metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (was 25)
- amlodipine 5 mg daily
- furosemide 40 mg daily
- tenofovir DF 300 mg daily
- acyclovir 400 mg twice daily
- daratumumab every 4 weeks (oncology)

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiology 4-6 weeks. Cardiac rehab information given.
Allergies: NKDA.

Cardiology

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u, inferior STEMI 11/5 with RCA stent. Discharge summary and cath report reviewed.

He was at a friend's birthday and used cocaine; pain started within the hour. No chest pain since discharge. Walking around the block. Has nitro, hasn't needed it. Scared - says he's done with cocaine. Still smoking a pack a day.
Taking all new meds. Ticagrelor copay issue at pharmacy - Medicaid wants a prior auth; he got a 7-day emergency supply.

Exam: BP and HR as charted. Radial site clean, no hematoma, good pulse. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.

A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p DES to RCA - DAPT (aspirin + ticagrelor), atorvastatin 80, metoprolol 50, nitro prn. Starting PA for ticagrelor today. Cardiology 4-6 weeks. Encouraged cardiac rehab.
2. Cocaine use disorder - this is the conversation to have; he's open. Discussed counseling resources; he'll think about it.
3. Tobacco - this is the moment to quit; not ready for a date.
4. CKD 4 - BMP today post contrast.
5. Myeloma - dara resumes next week per oncology.

RTC 6 weeks.

documents.author: RN

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Jackson five weeks after his cocaine-associated inferior STEMI treated with a mid-RCA drug-eluting stent.

He has had no angina and has not used nitroglycerin. No palpitations; no atrial fibrillation since the one episode in October 2022, and none on inpatient telemetry. He reports no cocaine since the event. Still smoking a pack a day.

Exam: BP and HR at goal. Heart regular, soft apical systolic murmur consistent with his mitral repair. Lungs clear.

Plan:
- Aspirin plus ticagrelor for 12 months, then aspirin alone.
- Atorvastatin 80 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg.
- Anticoagulation for AF: not now. Single remote episode, on dual antiplatelet therapy, advanced CKD; will revisit when DAPT ends.
- Cardiac rehab: he will try.
- Return in 6 months.

Cardiology

Myeloma: daratumumab monthly, oncology says still in very good response.

Exam: BP 130/80. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, soft apical systolic murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Trace ankle edema. Skin normal.
PHQ-2 1.

A/P
- CAD, old inferior MI, s/p DES - DAPT until November, then aspirin alone per cardiology. LDL on atorvastatin today.
- Paroxysmal AF - none since 2022.
- CKD 4 (FSGS, cast nephropathy) - CMP.
- Myeloma on maintenance.
- Hep B - tenofovir.
- HTN - goal.
- Cocaine/opioid use disorder - reports abstinence, supportive.
- Tobacco - counseled again.
- HM: flu/COVID 10/2024. Colon cancer screening starts at 45.

documents.body:
ED NOTE

41M with cocaine use disorder and an inferior STEMI last year, now with abrupt, severe, sharp chest pain he calls 'tearing,' going straight through to his back. Used cocaine earlier today.

BP 180/110, HR 105, RR 22. Diaphoretic, in obvious distress. Breath sounds diminished on the left. Extremities cool, capillary refill delayed.

Portable CXR: widened mediastinum, small left effusion. Bedside echo: intimal flap in the ascending aorta.
CTA chest: type A dissection.

IV esmolol and nicardipine started. Cardiac surgery at bedside; to OR emergently. Ticagrelor last dose this morning - surgery and blood bank aware.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Cardiac Surgery
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admitted 10/30/2025, discharged 11/12/2025

Diagnosis: acute Stanford type A aortic dissection, cocaine-associated.
Procedure 10/30/2025: emergent replacement of the ascending aorta with hemiarch repair under circulatory arrest; redo sternotomy (prior mitral repair).

Course: Taken to the OR from the ED. Platelet transfusion for recent ticagrelor. Extubated POD 1. ICU 4 days. Creatinine rose after surgery and settled near 3.8; no dialysis. Mitral repair inspected intraoperatively, intact. No atrial fibrillation during the stay. Ticagrelor stopped - he was within days of finishing 12 months of DAPT; aspirin continues. Metoprolol increased for strict blood pressure and heart rate control.

Discharge medications:
- CHANGED metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily
- STOPPED ticagrelor
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 80 mg nightly
- amlodipine 5 mg daily
- furosemide 40 mg daily
- nitroglycerin SL prn
- tenofovir DF 300 mg daily
- acyclovir 400 mg twice daily
- daratumumab: oncology to decide when to resume
- acetaminophen as needed for incision pain

Target BP under 120/80. No lifting over 10 lb for 8 weeks. No cocaine - another dissection or heart attack could be fatal.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiac surgery 4 weeks, cardiology.
Allergies: NKDA.

Cardiac Surgery
